tier_reason: The numbers are on the independent mloskot/json_benchmark README (VC++ 11.0 32-bit, Xeon E5-2687W, b2 variant=release), but the libjson rows cannot be reproduced from the public code: benchmark_libjson.cpp has a single commit (6593fd4, 2013-04-17) whose get_json() loads only canada.json, at HEAD it calls jb::get_json() which no longer exists in json_benchmark.hpp, and libjson has no Jamroot target, so the small-set harness and libjson's build options (JSONOptions.h, e.g. JSON_PREPARSE) are absent from public sources. That matches the rule that numbers built with flags absent from public sources are tier C; the win is also only 1.09x on one compiler.

corrections.stars_or_usage: SourceForge rating 4.8/5 from 47 reviews; 176 downloads per week (SourceForge page, 2026-10-07)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Visual C++ 11.0 (32-bit); benchmark programs built with Boost.Build 'b2 variant=release' (no explicit flags listed). libjson is not a target in the Jamroot, so how libjson was built and which JSONOptions.h options were set (JSON_PREPARSE on or off) is not stated.
corrections.workload: mloskot/json_benchmark 'small' set: data/one-json-per-line.jsons, 500 sample JSON strings from sub-100 to 500 characters, each parsed into the library's DOM type, 1000 iterations, best and worst of 2 marks; libjson against JsonCpp, RapidJSON (DOM mode), casablanca and JSON Spirit on VC++ 11.0 32-bit. The libjson harness only calls libjson::parse and checks the top-level node type.
corrections.caveats: Only numbers are from an independent 2013 hobby benchmark (mloskot/json_benchmark, 39 stars) whose author says it is not maintained and was superseded by Native JSON Benchmark; Native JSON Benchmark itself does not include this libjson (only vincenthz/libjson). The libjson rows are not reproducible from the published code: benchmark_libjson.cpp was never updated after its first commit, its get_json() loaded only canada.json (the small-set line is commented out), it calls a function missing from the current header, and libjson has no Jamroot target, so the small-set libjson run needed an unpublished local edit and an unstated libjson build. libjson 7.6.1's default JSONOptions.h leaves JSON_PREPARSE off, so libjson::parse is lazy by default and the benchmark only inspects the top-level type; the README gives a separate lazy-mode line (0.478065 to 0.486636 s) but never says which build produced the 5.2787 s row. The win over JsonCpp is about 1.09x (derived from page data) on VC++ 11.0 32-bit only; libjson was not measured on GCC 4.7, and on the large canada.json set libjson took 240.289 s vs RapidJSON 7.97 s with no JsonCpp row. The SourceForge page's own claim ('usually runs circles around other JSON libraries') has no numbers. Licence is the 2-clause BSD text (FreeBSD variant with the 'views and conclusions' clause) in License.txt of libjson_7.6.1.zip, Copyright 2010 Jonathan Wallace. Last release libjson_7.6.1.zip was uploaded 2012-06-25 and there is no public VCS; the SourceForge 'Last Update' 2016-11-09 is project-page activity. A 5-year-old SourceForge discussion post reports a GCC 9 build failure (std::map allocator value_type static assertion). This is a different project from vincenthz/libjson.

notes: Numbers in claimed_speedup match the README exactly, including the lazy-mode and large-set lines. Downgraded B to C because the libjson rows came from an unpublished harness edit and an unstated libjson build configuration, the margin over JsonCpp is 1.09x on one compiler, and RapidJSON beats libjson 5.5x on the same page. Licence verified from the release zip as BSD-2-Clause, so usability moves to copyable; last code release is 2012-06-25 (abandoned).
